narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 64% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt—meaning failure was judged more likely than success. The strongest factor was your third-year class-rank decile of 2, far below the accepted-student average of about 5.79; this pushed the prediction toward failure. Your LSAT score of 25, compared with an accepted-student average of about 37.18, was the second most influential factor and also pushed toward failure. The third most influential factor was your upper-middle family-income background, which worked in your favor and pushed toward passing; upper-middle income was also common among accepted students. It was not enough to offset the academic indicators. To improve your chances, focus on raising your LSAT score, strengthening your academic record through additional coursework or a rigorous post-baccalaureate program, and seek admissions advising about schools and pathways where your profile is more competitive. Reapply only after you can show clear evidence of improved readiness for law study and bar success.
